evidence: src/domain/errors.ts: DomainError is the abstract base class. ValidationError, NotFoundError, InsufficientStockError and InvalidTransitionError all extend it and are the only errors order.ts and product.ts throw.
src/domain/order.ts: LIFECYCLE and CANCELLABLE are defined once and used only through nextState(), isCancellable, advanceTo() and cancel().
src/domain/product.ts: reserve() calls ensureAvailable(), so the available-stock rule (onHand - reserved) has a single home.
src/domain/repositories.ts: ProductRepository and OrderRepository are typed against the domain aggregates Product, Order and OrderState. Clock and IdGenerator are also declared here as domain ports.

Minor: Order.place checks Number.isInteger(line.quantity) && quantity > 0 inline, while product.ts has its own assertPositiveInteger(). These are the same check, applied to order lines in one case and stock operations in the other.
Minor: Product.release and Product.dispatch each repeat the 'quantity > this.reserved' guard.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The four files make up one domain model for orders and inventory. errors.ts defines the DomainError hierarchy. order.ts holds the Order aggregate and its lifecycle state machine. product.ts holds the Product aggregate and its stock reservation rules. repositories.ts declares the ports to persistence and other outside dependencies. Each aggregate uses the module's own abstractions consistently: errors are always DomainError subclasses, construction goes through private constructors and factories (Order.place, Product.create), and state is exposed as read-only snapshots. Each lifecycle rule has one home: LIFECYCLE and CANCELLABLE in order.ts, and available, reserve and dispatch in product.ts. Three small issues don't amount to a real split or a meaningful duplicated invariant. First, the positive-integer quantity check appears twice: inline in Order.place and in assertPositiveInteger in product.ts. Second, the 'quantity > reserved' guard is repeated in Product.release and Product.dispatch. Third, Clock and IdGenerator are declared in a file named repositories.ts, but they are still domain ports, so this is a naming issue rather than a split in concerns.
